text:
maya: Heads-up — we've got at least two customer reports of double charges when clients retry after a 408/timeout. Looks like the retry sent same payload + no idempotency-key. Any ideas on guardrails?

sam: Ugh. Are they using per-org quotas or per-key? Double-charge usually from increment-on-accept + client retry.

maya: Per-org usage bucket. The sequence is client gets a 408 because upstream took long, client retries immediately, request completes second time and both attempts counted. No idempotency header present.

jonah: Two axes here: client-side idempotency headers (Idempotency-Key) and server-side lease/reservation semantics. We should decide if we charge at receipt or commit.

li: Charging at commit avoids this but means we need to reserve quota while request in-flight otherwise two simultaneous requests could both reserve and then both commit -> still double-charge.

sam: Right. We could implement a short-lived reservation token: on accept, do reserve_quota(org, amount, ttl) -> returns lease_id; if retry happens with same Idempotency-Key we reattach to lease. If final commit succeeds consume reservation, else release.

maya: But clients aren't sending Idempotency-Key consistently. Do we default to client IP + payload hash? That smells risky/privacy-wise and could cause false matches.

jonah: I think we should do conservative defaults: 1) Require/encourage Idempotency-Key in SDKs + console docs and add telemetry spikes to highlight missing keys. 2) Implement server-side reservation for short-running requests (<= 30s) and only decrement on commit. For long-running tasks we can do provisional reserves with a configurable max reservation window.

sam: Implementation detail: token-bucket counter + reservation map. Pseudocode: 
```
reserve_quota(org, units, ttl) -> lease_id
if available_units >= units:
  available_units -= units (temporarily)
  reservations[lease_id] = {units, expires_at}
  return lease_id
else:
  return insufficient_capacity

commit_lease(lease_id) -> mark consumed
release_lease(lease_id) -> available_units += units
```
This prevents two succeeds counting if they both try to reserve the same units but no idempotency.

li: What about burst controls? We have burst tokens for short spikes. If two retries happen in a burst, reservations might still be granted and then both commit -> we need to lock by idempotency when available. Maybe treat reservations + idempotency as best-effort: reservations reduce available_units, but on commit we check if a prior commit already consumed the same idempotency-key.

maya: So flow: if Idempotency-Key present -> use ledger keyed by (org, key) to dedupe commit. If not -> use reservation only. Also surface in billing that "provisional reservations" may be refunded if released (and show in console).

billing-bot: Billing event: "reservation_created" emitted when reserve_quota called (not billed). "reservation_committed" emitted on commit. "reservation_released" on release/refund.

sam: We should update the Quotas dashboard to show active reservations per org + reservation age histogram and add alert when reservation hold > 30s.

jonah: Edge case: clients that do exponential backoff but reuse the same connection and the SDK auto-retries without Idempotency-Key. We should update SDK default to attach a stable Idempotency-Key per logical request.

li: Agree. Also add an admin console control: "decrement-on-accept" toggle for legacy customers who want simpler semantics, with warnings about retry double-charges.

maya: Action items: 1) sam to draft reservation API (reserve/commit/release) + events schema for billing; 2) jonah to add idempotency ledger and server-side dedupe on commit; 3) li to update Quotas dashboard mockups to include reservations; 4) SDK owners to default Idempotency-Key usage.

sam: I'll open a RFC and a small spike branch. Going to include perf numbers: reservation map memory cost and worst-case leaks.

maya: Thanks. If someone sees live incidents, ping me + billing-bot.

jonah: Quick note: remember backing off auto-commit windows for streaming responses where tokens are billed per-token. Reservation model for streaming is trickier — might need rolling reservations.

li: Yep — we'll flag streaming as separate follow-up.

maya: OK closing loop here — let's sync on RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
